{{legend0|#D3D3D3|No election}} }} '''United States gubernatorial elections''' were held on November 2, 2021, in two states, [[New Jersey]] and [[Virginia]], and a recall election was held in [[California]] on September 14. These elections form part of the [[2021 United States elections]]. The last gubernatorial elections for New Jersey and Virginia were in [[2017 United States gubernatorial elections|2017]], and the last regular gubernatorial election for California was in [[2018 United States gubernatorial elections|2018]]. Going into the elections, all three seats were held by [[Democratic Party (US)|Democrats]]. In [[Virginia]], term-limited incumbent [[Ralph Northam]] was succeeded by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] businessman [[Glenn Youngkin]]. In [[New Jersey]], incumbent [[Phil Murphy]] won re-election. In [[California]], an unsuccessful special election to recall incumbent [[Gavin Newsom]] was held on September 14, 2021.{{cite web|url=https://ltg.ca.gov/2021/07/01/lieutenant-governor-kounalakis-declares-special-election/|title=Lieutenant Governor Kounalakis Declares Special Election|publisher=Office of the [[Lieutenant Governor of California]]|last=Kounalakis|first=Eleni|author-link=Eleni Kounalakis|date=July 1, 2021|access-date=July 1, 2021}}{{cite news|last1=Korte|first1=Lara|title=Gavin Newsom recall election date set: California voters to cast ballots in September|url=https://www.sacbee.com/news/politics-government/capitol-alert/article252113268.html|work=The Sacramento Bee|date=July 1, 2021|access-date=July 1, 2021}} This was the first time since [[1981 United States gubernatorial elections|1981]] that every regular gubernatorial election in this cycle was won by single digits, and the first time since [[1977 United States gubernatorial elections|1977]] that Democrats won in New Jersey and Republicans won in Virginia at the same time. As of {{CURRENTYEAR}}, this is the last time that Republicans won the governorship in Virginia. ==Election predictions== Several sites and individuals published predictions of competitive seats. These predictions looked at factors such as the strength of the [[incumbent]] (if the incumbent is running for re-election), the strength of the candidates, and the partisan leanings of the state (reflected in part by the state's [[Cook Partisan Voting Index]] rating). The predictions assigned ratings to each seat, with the rating indicating a party's predicted advantage in winning that seat. Most election predictors use: * "tossup": no advantage * "tilt" (used by some predictors): advantage that is not quite as strong as "lean" * "lean": slight advantage * "likely": significant, but surmountable, advantage * "safe" or "solid": near-certain chance of victory {|class="wikitable sortable" |- valign=bottom ! In 2020 and 2021, a recall petition gained momentum due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in California]] and Newsom's responses, eventually triggering a recall election.{{Cite web|last=Martichoux|first=Alix|date=February 3, 2021|title=Why do people want to recall Gov. Gavin Newsom? We explain|url=https://abc7.com/10256979/|access-date=February 11, 2021|website=ABC7 Los Angeles|language=en}}{{Cite web|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/543955-whats-next-in-the-california-recall|title=What's next in the California recall|last=Wilson|first=Reid|date=March 19, 2021|website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]|access-date=March 25, 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210319221549/https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/543955-whats-next-in-the-california-recall|archive-date=March 19, 2021}} The ballot featured two questions, whether to recall Newsom and who would have replaced him if he had been recalled. Newsom was ineligible to run as a candidate for the second question. The election was the fourth gubernatorial recall election in American history and the second in state history after the [[2003 California gubernatorial recall election|2003 recall election]], which resulted in the successful recall of Governor [[Gray Davis]], who was replaced with [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]]. A large number of candidates announced their intention to replace Newsom. Among the most prominent Republicans in the race included [[2018 California gubernatorial election|2018 Republican nominee]] [[John H. Cox]], former [[San Diego]] [[Mayor of San Diego|mayor]] [[Kevin Faulconer]], media personalities [[Caitlyn Jenner]] and [[Larry Elder]], in addition to former [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representative]] [[Doug Ose]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.foxnews.com/politics/john-cox-challenge-californias-newsom-recall-effort-succeeds|title=John Cox says he'll challenge California's Newsom if recall effort succeeds|last=Phillips|first=Morgan|date=January 30, 2021|website=[[Fox News]]|access-date=February 1, 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210203075938/https://www.foxnews.com/politics/john-cox-challenge-californias-newsom-recall-effort-succeeds|archive-date=February 3, 2021}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/states/california/story/2021/02/01/former-san-diego-mayor-officially-announces-gop-challenge-to-newsom-1361429|title=Former San Diego mayor to officially launch GOP challenge to Newsom|first=Carla|last=Marinucci|date=February 1, 2021|website=[[Politico]]|access-date=February 1, 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210203080117/https://www.politico.com/states/california/story/2021/02/01/former-san-diego-mayor-officially-announces-gop-challenge-to-newsom-1361429|archive-date=February 3, 2021}}{{Cite web|last3= Swan|first3= Jonathan|first1= Lachlan|last1= Markay|first2 =Alayna|last2 =Treene|title=Caitlyn Jenner files paperwork to run for governor of California|url=https://www.axios.com/caitlyn-jenner-california-governor-run-710153ef-7a89-460d-b9ec-9efed2a9399f.html|access-date=2021-04-23|website=Axios|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=Blood|first=Michael R.|date=March 16, 2021|title=Former GOP Rep. 2021 California gubernatorial election.title: 2021 California gubernatorial recall election
2021 California gubernatorial election.text:
{{Short description|Recall election in US state}} {{see also|2021 United States gubernatorial elections}} {{Use American English|date=January 2025}} {{Use mdy dates|date=September 2021}} {{Infobox election | election_name = 2021 California gubernatorial recall election | country = California | type = presidential | ongoing = no | previous_election = 2018 California gubernatorial election | previous_year = 2018 | next_election = 2022 California gubernatorial election | next_year = 2022 | election_date = September 14, 2021{{cite web|url=https://electionresults.sos.ca.gov/returns/governor-recall|title=Recall Question – Statewide Results|date=September 14, 2021|access-date=September 14, 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2021/results/california|title=California Recall Newsom Recall Vote|date=September 15, 2021|access-date=September 15, 2021}} | turnout = 58.45% ({{decrease}}4.83 [[Percentage point|pp]]) | module = {{Infobox referendum | embed = yes |name=Vote on recall |no=7,944,092 |yes=4,894,474 |total= 12,838,566 |electorate=22,057,154 |turnoutpct=58.45 |map={{Switcher | [[File:2021 California gubernatorial recall election referendum results map by county.svg|300px]] | County results | [[File:2021 California gubernatorial recall election results map by congressional district.svg|300px]] | Congressional district results}} |question=Shall Gavin Newsom be recalled (removed) from the office of Governor? |map_caption= '''No''': {{legend0|#DEDEBD|50–60%}} {{legend0|#BCBC83|60–70%}} {{legend0|#8B8B54|70–80%}} {{legend0|#5D5D2D|80–90%}} {{legend0|#32320C|>90%}}
'''Yes''': {{legend0|#B6C8D9|50–60%}} {{legend0|#7D9CBB|60–70%}} {{legend0|#47729E|70–80%}} {{legend0|#28497C|80–90%}} |module= {{Infobox election | embed = yes | election_name = Replacement candidates | type = by-election | seats_for_election = If Newsom is recalled, who should replace him as governor? | image_size = 150x150px | image1 = Larry Elder (53424050545) (cropped).jpg | candidate1 = [[Larry Elder]] | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | popular_vote1 = 3,563,867 | percentage1 = 48.41% | image2 = File:Kevin Paffrath (cropped).jpg | candidate2 = [[Kevin Paffrath]] | party2 = Democratic Party (United States) | popular_vote2 = 706,778 | percentage2 = 9.60% | image4 = File:Kevin Faulconer (cropped) (1).png | candidate4 = [[Kevin Faulconer]] | party4 = Republican Party (United States) | popular_vote4 = 590,346 | percentage4 = 8.02% | image5 = 3x4.svg | candidate5 = Brandon Ross | party5 = Democratic Party (United States) | popular_vote5 = 392,029 | percentage5 = 5.33% | map_image = {{Switcher | [[File:2021 California gubernatorial recall election replacement results map by county.svg|300px]] | County results | [[File:2021 California gubernatorial recall election replacement results map by congressional district.svg|300px]] | Congressional district results}} | map_caption = '''Elder''': {{legend0|#FFE0EA|20–30%}} {{legend0|#FFC8CD|30–40%}} {{legend0|#FFB2B2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#E27F7F|50–60%}} {{legend0|#D75D5D|60–70%}}
'''Paffrath''': {{legend0|#DFEEFF|20–30%}} | ongoing = no }} }} }} The '''2021 California gubernatorial recall election''' was a special [[recall election]] that started in August 2021 and ended on September 14, 2021, when the majority of California voters chose not to recall incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Governor [[Gavin Newsom]], elected for the term January 2019 to January 2023. Had the recall been successful, the replacement candidate with the most votes on the second part of the ballot would have assumed the office. The election followed the same format used in the [[2020 California elections|November 2020 general election]]: in August, county election offices sent an official ballot to the mailing address of every registered voter, giving them the option to [[vote by mail]] on or before [[election day]], or, when polling places opened statewide, to vote in-person.{{cite news|last1=Korte|first1=Lara|title=Gavin Newsom recall election date set: California voters to cast ballots in September|url=https://www.sacbee.com/news/politics-government/capitol-alert/article252113268.html|work=[[The Sacramento Bee]]|date=July 1, 2021|access-date=July 1, 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://calmatters.org/politics/2021/07/newsom-recall-election-date/|title=It's a date: Newsom recall election set for Sept. 14|date=July 1, 2021|website=CalMatters|first=Laurel|last=Rosenhall}} The recall petition was filed in February 2020 and signatures were collected from June 2020 to March 2021, with the signature drive gaining critical momentum in late 2020 regarding Newsom's personal behavior and leadership during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in California|COVID-19 pandemic]]. Voters' ability to recall an elected official in California is the result of [[Progressive Era]] democratic reforms intended to reduce corruption, enacted alongside the introduction of the [[California ballot proposition|ballot initiative]] and [[Women's suffrage in California|women's suffrage]] in 1911. Following a petition drive collecting signatures amounting to at least 12 percent of voters in the previous election for the political office in question, a special election is held. The election was the fourth gubernatorial recall election in American history and the second in state history after the [[2003 California gubernatorial recall election|2003 recall election]], which resulted in the successful recall of Governor [[Gray Davis]], who was replaced with [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]]. The ballot asked voters two separate questions: whether to recall Newsom as governor, and which candidate should replace Newsom as governor if he were recalled. All voters could answer the second question regardless of their vote (if any) on the first. Allies of Newsom were successful in dissuading any high-profile Democrats from entering the field of candidates seeking to replace Newsom if he was recalled. His campaign encouraged voters to vote "no" on the first question (whether to recall Newsom) while abstaining from voting on the second question (who should replace Newsom if he were recalled). Largely as consequence of this, while 12,838,565 voters answered the first question, only 7,361,568 voters answered the second. Due to the wide margin of the results, most major news outlets projected the race for Newsom within an hour of polls closing; later that night, [[Larry Elder]], the frontrunner replacement candidate, conceded defeat.{{Cite web|last=Blood|first=Michael R.|date=September 15, 2021|title=GOP's Elder concedes California recall, hints: 'Stay tuned'|url=https://apnews.com/article/california-recall-california-e4fdf2c9340c9ae65958fdb2de68f1f0|url-status=live|access-date=September 15, 2021|website=[[Associated Press]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210915080729/https://apnews.com/article/california-recall-california-e4fdf2c9340c9ae65958fdb2de68f1f0 |archive-date=September 15, 2021 }} Official certification of the results occurred on October 22, 2021. == Background == {{Elections in California sidebar}} Following their ascension into power in 1911, California's [[progressive Republican]] reformers introduced [[direct democracy]] with the recall ([[1911 California Proposition 8|Proposition 8]]) and the initiative and referendum ([[1911 California Proposition 7|Proposition 7]]) processes, alongside other sweeping democratic reforms like women's suffrage ([[1911 California Proposition 4|Proposition 4]]),{{cite web|url=https://www.vox.com/22617048/california-recall-gavin-newsom-larry-elder|website=[[Vox (website)|Vox]]|title=How California's bizarre recall system could elect a Republican governor|first=Andrew|last=Prokop|date=August 23, 2021}} to weaken the corrupting power of private interests over the state's government (especially that of the enormously influential [[Southern Pacific Railroad]]), and restore, according to newly elected governor [[Hiram Johnson]], "the people's rule".{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/08/18/opinion/newsom-recall-california.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210818160634/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/08/18/opinion/newsom-recall-california.html |archive-date=2021-08-18 |url-access=limited|website=[[The New York Times]]|title=Why Deep Blue California Could Elect a Bright Red Governor|first=Kathryn|last=Olmsted|date=August 18, 2021}} Prior to this election, the only other gubernatorial recall attempt in California to qualify for the ballot happened in 2003, which resulted in [[Gray Davis]] being replaced by [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]].{{cite web|last=Navarro|first=Aaron|date=February 1, 2021|title=Recall threats are common in California. But the latest one against Gavin Newsom might get further than most|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/gavin-newsom-recall-california-governor/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210203074119/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/gavin-newsom-recall-california-governor/|archive-date=February 3, 2021|access-date=February 2, 2021|website=[[CBS News]]}}{{cite web|last=Lozano|first=Alicia Victoria|date=December 20, 2020|title=California governor faces recall effort amid pandemic, dining at famed French Laundry|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/recall-effort-against-california-governor-attempt-destabilize-political-system-analysts-n1251498|access-date=May 10, 2021|website=[[NBC News]]|language=en}} This election was the result of one of 179 attempts to recall a state-level elected official in California since voters gained the right to recall in 1911, one of 55 attempts to recall a governor, and one of six such efforts to remove Newsom.{{cite web|title=Recall History in California (1913 to Present)|url=https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/recalls/recall-history-california-1913-present|website=[[California Secretary of State]]}} Every California governor since 1960 has experienced some form of a recall attempt.{{Cite news|last=Abruzzese|first=Sarah|date=February 19, 2021|title=Gavin Newsom and the Coronavirus-Driven California Recall Effort|website=[[U.S. News & World Report|US News]]|url=https://www.usnews.com/news/elections/articles/2021-02-19/gavin-newsom-and-the-coronavirus-driven-california-recall-effort}} Of the ten prior recall attempts on state-level elected officials in California which led to special recall elections, six ultimately resulted in their removal from office by voters. The recall election was the fourth gubernatorial recall election ever held in the United States;{{cite web|last1=Brownstein|first1=Ronald|date=May 13, 2021|title=The Trouble With the Gavin Newsom Recall|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/politics/archive/2021/05/newsom-recall-california/618872/|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=[[The Atlantic]]}} the other three were in [[1921 North Dakota gubernatorial recall election|North Dakota in 1921]], [[2003 California gubernatorial recall election|California in 2003]], and [[2012 Wisconsin gubernatorial recall election|Wisconsin in 2012]]. === Newsom recall petition (June 2020 – March 2021) === [[File:Gavin Newsom by Gage Skidmore.jpg|thumb|Newsom in 2019|left|200x200px]] During Newsom's tenure as governor, a total of seven recall petitions have been launched against him. On February 20, 2020, the petition which led to the 2021 recall election was served against Newsom. It stated, "People in this state suffer the highest taxes in the nation, the highest homelessness rates, and the lowest quality of life as a result."{{cite web |title=PETITION FOR RECALL |url=https://rescuecalifornia.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/Recall_Gavin_Petition_8.5x11_2021_FINAL.pdf |website=rescuecalifornia.org |access-date=April 13, 2021 |archive-date=January 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210129163247/https://rescuecalifornia.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/Recall_Gavin_Petition_8.5x11_2021_FINAL.pdf |url-status=dead }} The timing of the recall attempt coincided with the onset of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in California|COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/12/14/politics/gavin-newsom-recall-california-governor-2021/index.html|title=How it all went so wrong for Gavin Newsom|last=Cillizza|first=Chris|author-link=Chris Cillizza|date=December 15, 2020|website=[[CNN]]|access-date=December 16, 2020|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210203074734/https://www.cnn.com/2020/12/14/politics/gavin-newsom-recall-california-governor-2021/index.html|archive-date=February 3, 2021}} The basis for previous recall attempts included the state's "[[Universal Healthcare]] and laws regarding illegal aliens" and "homelessness".{{cite web |title=Gavin Newsom recall, Governor of California (2019–2021) |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Gavin_Newsom_recall,_Governor_of_California_(2019-2021) |website=[[Ballotpedia]] |access-date=May 9, 2021 |language=en}}{{cite web |title=PETITION FOR RECALL |url=https://takecaback.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/TakeCABack-Petition-to-Recall-Newsom.pdf |website=takecaback.org}}{{cite web |last1=Marinucci |first1=Carla |title=Long shot Newsom recall drive gets serious in California |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2020/12/16/newsom-recall-california-447019 |website=[[Politico]] |access-date=April 15, 2021 |language=en |date=December 16, 2020|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210203074703/https://www.politico.com/news/2020/12/16/newsom-recall-california-447019|archive-date=February 3, 2021}} On June 10, 2020, then–[[Secretary of State of California|Secretary of State]] [[Alex Padilla]] approved petitioners' petitions for circulation. The recall petition focused on a variety of grievances, on issues such as [[Sanctuary city#United States|sanctuary policies]], homelessness, high taxes, and water rationing.{{cite web|url=https://recallgavin2020.com/petition/|title=Official Recall Petition|website=recallgavin2020.com|access-date=August 3, 2021|archive-date=August 19, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210819141430/https://recallgavin2020.com/petition/}} Newsom's official response to the petition touted his support for funding education, health care, and infrastructure, noted the State's fiscal health, and warned that the recall campaign was a partisan attack that would result in a costly election. The recall campaign hired a political consulting firm in late June 2020, and the initial plan was to pay circulators to collect signatures. To ensure a successful validation, the recall campaign sought to gather 2 million signatures.{{cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/states/california/story/2021/02/19/newsom-recall-drive-faces-tight-finish-based-on-latest-california-data-9425479|title=Newsom recall drive faces tight finish based on latest California data|first=Jeremy B.|last=White|work=[[Politico]]|date=February 19, 2021|access-date=February 21, 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210220013929/https://www.politico.com/states/california/story/2021/02/19/newsom-recall-drive-faces-tight-finish-based-on-latest-california-data-9425479|archive-date=February 20, 2021}}{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2021/02/gavin-newsom-recall-million-signatures-1234697678/|title=Gavin Newsom Recall Effort Delivers 1M Signatures To California Elections Officials|first=Tom|last=Tapp|work=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]]|date=February 19, 2021|access-date=February 21, 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210220024901/https://deadline.com/2021/02/gavin-newsom-recall-million-signatures-1234697678/|archive-date=February 20, 2021}} Given the difficulties in obtaining signatures during the pandemic, however, the per-signature cost rose dramatically, and petitioners opted to proceed with a team of approximately 5,000 volunteer circulators instead. The first proponent of the recall, Orrin Heatlie, played a grassroots role in the previous attempt led by aspiring [[Tea Party movement|Tea Party]] politician Erin Cruz.{{cite news |last1=Ronayne |first1=Kathleen |title=Meet Orrin Heatlie, the ex-cop leading the push to recall California Gov.
